methodology: Real registerMemoryApi; one writer in a dedicated host process and an independent HTTP client process.
Native timing wraps the existing writer's consoleRequest; write timing separately records flush.
Concurrent ping uses the real GET /status endpoint; concurrent writes use POST /nodes/:id and require exact acknowledged payload visibility.

Baseline phases send only the same HTTP writes and status pings, without concurrent TQL. Baseline latencies are reported separately; the experiment does not claim a statistically controlled incremental-overhead estimate.
Event-loop lag includes synchronous queries and confirmed write flushes; it is not attributed exclusively to TQL.
Deadlines are observed, not assumed: a 1ms probe may finish before cancellation; outcomes retain success, budget rejection and deadline cancellation separately.

Small-fixture full-input pagination must succeed. Large full-input pagination may explicitly exceed native work budgets; rejected requests are counted separately and never described as successful pagination.
Both fixture sizes must successfully sort/page a parameter-filtered 64-node working set, with exact expected ranks 1..20 and 21..40 verified independently of the returned ordering.
